subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Acme)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Acme)

Hi Alicia / Ben -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Wanted to recap the key pricing/volume points and next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: end-user chat + a suite of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flows.
- Expected monthly token mix: ~70% prompts + 30% outputs; peak daily queries around 20k/day.
- Target monthly volume (initial): 50M-150M tokens; potential to scale after Q3.

Pricing / unit economics notes from Acme: 
- Acme target effective pricing: looking for ~$1,250-$1,750 per 1M tokens (goal is to be cost-competitive with hosted vendors while preserving quality).
- Current commercial benchmarks: Acme is seeing OpenAI list at roughly $2,400/1M (for the models discussed) and Anthropic at ~$2,200/1M; some open-model hosts are in the $900-$1,200/1M range but require additional infra and ops investment.

What I'll do next: 
- Share a short target-price benchmarking sheet (attached) comparing Redwood vs OpenAI / Anthropic / common open-model hosts across unit $/1M tokens, expected latency, and SLA tiers.
- Request permission to run a 48-72 hour pilot benchmark (no production data) to measure token efficiency and latency for your RAG prompts - this will let us estimate realized $/1M under your workload.
- Loop in Neha (copied) to scope any engineering prerequisites for the pilot and to prepare a tailored pricing plan if the pilot looks good.

Asks for you: 
1) Can you confirm a target $/1M token range you'd need to see to move forward (you mentioned ~$1.25k-$1.75k on the call - please confirm)?
2) Do we have sign-off to run the short benchmark on a sanitized subset of production queries?
3) Any procurement timing / budget windows we should be aware of for June/July?

Attachments: redwood-pricing-1m-token-comparison.xlsx, mutual-action-plan-Acme.pdf

Thanks - happy to jump back on a quick 30-min sync if easier.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Acme)

Thanks Vanessa - great recap and appreciate the spreadsheet. Quick answers below: 

1) Target price: yes, our procurement comfort range for a hosted/managed partner is ~$1,250-$1,750 per 1M tokens. Tighter goal would be to land near the $1,250 mark if performance and SLAs are comparable to the incumbents.
2) Pilot: we're okay to proceed with a 48-72 hour benchmark on a sanitized query set. I'll need a short DPIA & data handling note outlining how Redwood will sanitize and store logs for the test.
3) Timing: budget is provisioned for H2; we're prioritizing vendor selection in June. If we can get a benchmark and a preliminary commercial, we can accelerate to procurement during the second half of June.

A couple of clarifying points: 
- Our current monthly baseline estimate (after the POC) is ~80M tokens/month; with aggressive adoption could reach ~200M by EOY.
- We absolutely care about tail latency: 95th p95 targets should be sub-600ms for the interactive flows.

Ben - FYI on the pilot and pricing targets.

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Head of Product, AI Platforms
Acme Retail
alicia@acme.com

> Hi Alicia / Ben -
>

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Acme)

Thanks for the quick confirmation, Alicia - that's very helpful. A couple follow-ups & next steps: 

Pilot scope & DPIA: Neha - can you draft a short DPIA/data handling note (1 page) that explains: what gets sanitized, retention for the pilot logs, and where keys are stored? We'll attach to the pilot kickoff doc for Acme.

Benchmark plan (48-72h):
- We'll run the benchmark against a sanitized subset (~5-10k representative queries) of your RAG prompt patterns.
- Metrics we'll capture: realized tokens per request (prompt vs completion), latency P50/P95, model quality delta vs baseline, GPU utilization and estimated $/1M tokens under continuous load.
- Goal is to produce a short report with an expected realized $/1M token for your workload and a recommended pricing band for Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted options.

Commercial ask: based on the volumes you quoted (80M starting, 200M EOY upside), our initial target to be competitive is $1,200/1M tokens for a mid-tier SLA - this puts Redwood between open-model hosts (cheap but ops heavy) and the big-host incumbents. We'll be explicit in the pilot report how that number maps to token mix and latency/availability targets.

Next steps & timing:
- Neha to send DPIA + pilot runbook by EOD today.
- Acme to confirm sanitized query subset (shared Drive link or secure upload).
- Pilot to start as soon as we have sanitized data and NDA ok (goal: start by 2027-06-03).

Alicia - does that timeline work for you? If so I'll lock Neha on the kickoff and we'll prepare the pilot environment.

Thanks -
Vanessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Acme)

Thanks Vanessa - I'll get the DPIA and pilot runbook over today.

Quick note on the commercial math (so Acme has visibility):
- Baseline assumptions: 80M tokens/month -> at $1,200/1M => ~$96k/month (recurring).
- Upside (200M) -> at $1,200/1M => ~$240k/month.
- If we can demonstrate token efficiency (e.g., 10-20% fewer tokens for your prompts vs baseline), realized unit-costs move in your favor and can get closer to the $1,000/1M effective range.

I'll include a short table in the runbook with sample math across 3 tiers (hosted starter, hosted production, dedicated).

-Neha
